```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

`qtlpost` works on the standard outputs of the qtl-pipeline Snakemake
workflow (see `docs/output_contract.md` in the pipeline repository): the
annotated permutation table per phenotype set, the nominal associations of
FDR-significant phenotypes, and the phenotype annotation. The pipeline calls
the same functions for its batch runs; this vignette uses them interactively
on the bundled synthetic toy data (60 donors, two planted causal variants,
`rs_causal_1` and `rs_causal_2`).

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(qtlpost)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
ext <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "qtlpost")
```

## QTL results and FDR

Each row of a permutation table is one phenotype (here a cell-cell
interaction mapped at its ligand gene, set `cci_sending`, or at its receptor
gene, `cci_receiving`) with its lead variant, beta-approximated permutation
p-value and q-value.

```{r results}
qt <- rbind(fread(ext("cci_sending.permute.tsv.gz")), fread(ext("cci_receiving.permute.tsv.gz")))
gt <- read_group_table(ext("cell_types.tsv"))
qt[fdr_pass == TRUE, .(set, phenotype_id, group, gene, var_id, qval)][order(qval)][1:6]
```

q-values can be recomputed with a different stratification, e.g. one global
q-value instead of one per anchor subclass:

```{r requalify}
qt[, qval_global := qvalue_by_group(adj_beta_pval, rep("all", .N))]
qt[, .(per_group = sum(qval <= 0.05), global = sum(qval_global <= 0.05)), by = set]
```

```{r fdr-plot}
counts <- fdr_summary(qt, by = c("set", "group"))
plot_fdr_counts(counts, gt)
```

## Colocalisation with a GWAS

`run_coloc()` tests every phenotype in a nominal table against one GWAS and
classifies each colocalisation by how sharply it points at one SNP.

```{r coloc, message = FALSE}
nom <- fread(ext("cci_sending.nominal.fdr.tsv.gz"))
spec <- list(name = "TOY_CC", snp_col = "SNP", bp_col = "BP", beta_col = "beta", se_col = "se",
             p_col = "p", n_col = "N", type = "cc", s = 0.4)
gwas <- standardize_gwas(fread(ext("gwas_toy_cc.tsv.gz")), spec)
settings <- list(p1 = 1e-4, p2 = 1e-4, p12 = 1e-5, min_snps = 1, pp_h4 = 0.5, snp_pp_h4 = 0.1)
res <- run_coloc(nom, gwas, spec, n_qtl = 59, settings = settings, label = list(set = "cci_sending"))
res$summary[order(-PP.H4), .(phenotype_id, PP.H4, tier, lead_snp)][1:5]
```

```{r locus, fig.height = 7}
top <- res$summary[order(-PP.H4)][1]
d <- nom[phe_id == top$phenotype_id & var_id %chin% gwas$snp]
plot_locus(d, gwas[snp %chin% d$var_id], res$results[[top$phenotype_id]],
           title = top$phenotype_id, subtitle = sprintf("PP.H4 = %.3f", top$PP.H4),
           annot = read_annotation(ext("gene_annotation.tsv")),
           focus_gene = qt[phenotype_id == top$phenotype_id, gene][1])
```

## Choosing the number of hidden factors

With `sensitivity.sweep_k` the pipeline re-runs the permutation pass for each
number of hidden factors (e.g. PEER factors). Here, the toy CAGE-style data:

```{r ksweep}
sweep <- fread(ext("cage_sensitivity_summary.tsv"))
sweep <- sweep[set == "cage", .SD[1], by = .(set, k)]
plot_ksweep(sweep[, .(set, k, n_fdr_01, n_fdr_05, n_fdr_10)])
```

## Other functions

- `pi1_replication()`: replication of QTL hits in an eQTL resource
- `run_mediation()`: genotype → anchor expression → partner expression
- `phenotype_expression_cor()`: phenotype vs expression of its gene
- `magma_gene_sets()`, `read_magma_gsa()`, `plot_magma_heatmap()`: MAGMA gene-set analysis
- `plot_upset_classes()`, `plot_coloc_summary()`, `plot_chord()`: summary figures
